AST SpaceMobile, Inc. (NASDAQ:ASTS) shares fell about 6% on Wednesday as communications and satellite names sold off, with Space Exploration Technologies Corp. (NASDAQ:SPCX) dropping nearly 3%.

On Tuesday, ASTS had received backing from the U.S. and Japanese governments connected to its satellite partnership with Rakuten Group. The stock still trades well below a longer-term technical level flagged in that analysis.

The shares sit about 1.6% below their 20-day moving average of $60.15 and about 5.9% below the 50-day average of $62.89. They remain far below the 100-day ($73.10) and 200-day ($81.02) averages. The RSI is 48.08, which is neutral. A death cross formed in July, when the 50-day average fell below the 200-day average.

Key resistance is at $65.50 and key support at $57.50. At publication, ASTS was down 6.15% at $59.24. Over the past year the stock is down 20.7%, the weakest result in its peer group, while SPCX is up 558.8% over the same period.
headline: ASTS Slides 6% Wednesday in Sector-Wide Selloff Despite Recent Government Support
summary: AST SpaceMobile fell about 6% to $59.24 amid a sector selloff, still below its key moving averages despite recent government backing.
